answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 25 money. 2. Each player has 1 active association worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying below it. 3. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 in hand and discard 4 face up. 4. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden beside the zoo map. 5. Put the Animals Action card in the leftmost slot (strength 1); shuffle the other four cards among the remaining slots; all begin side I up. 6. Starting Appeal positions are staggered by turn order: first player 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C1–F: 25 money; one active and three inactive workers; draw 8/keep 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards; Animals in slot 1; appeal staggered 0–3.

answers.answer: 1. At setup, put 3 Base Conservation Project cards face up below the Association board in 2- or 3-player games, and 4 in a 4-player game. 2. In a 2-player game only, block one level on each of those three projects (left level on left card, middle on middle card, right on right card) and the three donation spaces in the left column; both players are barred from them. With 3 or 4 players none of those levels or donation spaces is blocked at setup. 3. Reveal the initial 6-card display only after everyone has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: Global setup 5b–5c states 4 projects in four players, otherwise 3, and details the two-player blocked spaces; personal setup G reveals display after hands are chosen.

answers.answer: 1. After using the card from slot 4, remove it, shift cards from slots 1–3 one slot right, and place the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before the action; each X-token spent adds +1 strength, and any number may be spent (though some actions cap their benefit). X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. 3. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 4. Resolve an “after finishing” effect after the action is complete, including moving the Action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove used card, shift cards left of the empty slot right, place used card in slot 1; strength is set before; each X-token +1, max 5; after-finishing effects follow card movement.

answers.answer: 1. You may not take a regular action that does nothing; playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not legal. 2. Instead, choose the X-token alternative: take exactly 1 X-token, use any Action card (its strength and upgrade state do not matter), move it to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right. 3. You cannot take this alternative while already holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says a turn cannot do nothing; X-token action section gives exactly 1 token, card movement and 5-token limit.

answers.answer: 1. When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional movement beyond that space and the player reaching it gains 1 X-token. 2. The break occurs after the triggering player finishes their current turn; that player completes the turn, then the break is performed. 3. After the break the token returns to its starting space and play resumes clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track: break after current turn; gain 1 X-token; ignore extra steps; after break return token to start; break procedure step 6 says continue clockwise with next player.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I always advances the Break token 2 spaces without money, then choose either the strength-table deck draw (maximum 3 cards, with any required discard) or, at strength 5+, snap exactly 1 display card of choice regardless of reputation and with no deck draw. 2. Cards II also advances the Break token 2 spaces, then allows deck draws and/or in-range display draws in any order according to its upgraded table; the display is not refilled until turn end. Its snap is available at strength 3+ and takes exactly 1 display card, with no deck draw. 3. The reputation restriction applies to Cards II's display-draw option, not to snapping. 4. The display is replenished at end of turn after display cards were taken. 5. Hand limit is not enforced during play; discard to it only at breaks (normally 3, or 5 with hand-limit university).
answers.evidence: Cards action lists both sides, snap rules and 2-space Break movement; Special Rules says display refill at turn end and hand size enforced only at breaks.

answers.answer: 1. “Within reputation range” means the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action. 3. At reputation 15, further reputation does not move the counter; gain 1 Appeal per remaining reputation step. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display defines range, Cards II requirement at 10+, conversion above 15, and prohibits inspecting discard pile.

answers.answer: 1. Build I builds exactly 1 building, size up to strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, never two identical buildings in one action. 2. Pay 2 money per space for each building, before placing it. 3. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. 4. Build only on empty map spaces, within the map, and not over water or rock; spaces with the restricted icon require Build II. 5. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion immediately increases Appeal by 1, once.
answers.evidence: Build action gives side limits and cost; placement rules specify first/later placement, restricted spaces and kiosk spacing; pavilion immediately adds 1 Appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Build I permits standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo (size 3). Build II additionally permits one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary (each size 5); each individual zoo may have only one of each special type. 2. The supply contains four tiles of each special enclosure for the four players. 3. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 4. With Build II, covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives 7 Appeal; this can also be triggered by another effect that covers the map.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table, special enclosure supply note, Build II says unique buildings only via Sponsor and full-map coverage grants 7 Appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. 2. Immediate effects resolve when triggered, including before a later animal or building step; “after finishing” effects wait until the whole action is complete and the Action card has moved. 3. If effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure allows earlier action benefits to be used later and requires payment before own benefits; animal/build timing and Special Rules specify immediate, after-finishing and simultaneous-effect order.

answers.answer: 1. To play an Animal, meet all its listed conditions, pay its cost first, and provide legal housing. A partner zoo matching each continent icon on that Animal reduces its cost by 3 money per icon (so two matching icons reduce it by 6). 2. In a standard enclosure, an eligible animal needs an empty enclosure at least its printed minimum size; admit one animal and flip the whole enclosure to occupied. Petting Zoo animals must go in a Petting Zoo. Reptiles and some birds may use the indicated Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary alternative; mark the indicated occupied spaces with one supply player token per space, and do not flip the special enclosure. 3. Meet any printed water/rock adjacency requirements for the selected enclosure; count distinct adjacent terrain hexes, including for special enclosures. 4. Pay before any money-gain effect from the play. Appeal and other ordinary effects resolve as each animal is played; “after finishing” effects wait until the Animals action and card movement are complete.
answers.evidence: Animals action steps 1–4 state conditions, full payment before effects, partner discount per icon, housing/occupancy and terrain adjacency; after-finishing timing is specified there.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II may play Animal cards from hand and from display folders within reputation range, in any mix; each display animal costs its folder number in addition to its printed cost. 2. At strength 5+, you may optionally gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action so the new range applies to animals played. 3. Do not replenish the display until the turn ends. 4. Animals II also permits animals whose conditions show the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: Animals II states display play/cost, optional reputation first at strength 5+, turn-end refill, and upgrade-required conditions.

answers.answer: 1. Only immediately when constructing a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you relocate suitable existing animals into that newly built enclosure; move all corresponding eligible animals that fit, choosing separately for each. 2. Mark each moved animal's indicated space requirement with that many player tokens from your supply; respect the new special enclosure's remaining capacity and terrain adjacency. 3. For each animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all that animal's requirements, including terrain. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size requirement, flip none. 4. This relocation is not release into the wild.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals section limits relocation to construction, requires eligible animals that fit, adds tokens, and gives the smallest-enclosure selection and fallback.

answers.answer: 1. Association tasks have strengths: increase reputation 2, gain partner zoo 3, gain university 4, conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task. Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total strength is no greater than the action strength, and may add at most one donation if at least one task was performed. 3. A task uses at least 1 active worker. If one of your workers is already on that task, place 2 workers to repeat it; if 3 of your workers are there, you cannot do it again before the break. 4. Other players' workers on the task do not affect your ability.
answers.evidence: Association action lists each task strength; side I and II limits, worker repeat rule and says other players' workers do not matter.

answers.answer: 1. Take partner zoos and universities from the available spaces on the Association board and put each on the lowest empty matching space on your zoo map. Resolve any covered-space bonus immediately; for a university also take its printed reputation award. 2. You cannot take a duplicate university. Partner zoos must represent different continents, with a maximum of 4; the third and fourth require Association II. 3. Partner zoos give the continent icon and reduce animal cost by 3 per matching continent icon. 4. Only the hand-limit university raises the normal hand limit from 3 to 5; the other universities do not change it.
answers.evidence: Association gain tasks and university table describe board-to-map placement, immediate bonuses/reputation, duplicates, partner limits/discounts, and hand-limit university.

answers.answer: 1. Conservation Project work may support an existing project or bring a Conservation Project card from hand into play and support it immediately; with Association II a new project may also come from an in-range display card for its folder-number cost. 2. Fulfill a printed condition and choose a level with no player token on it; each level holds one token total, and normally you may support each project only once. 3. Take a player token from the left edge of your zoo map, put it on the chosen condition, and gain that level's conservation/reputation reward. Removing it activates its map bonus; take that bonus immediately, in either order with the project reward (and again at breaks if it is recurring income). 4. New projects enter above the Association board. If the row exceeds its player-count limit, discard the rightmost card; return tokens on it to owners' supplies, while activated map bonuses stay active. Setup Base Conservation Projects below the board never move or replenish.
answers.evidence: Association conservation project work details entry, support limits and sequence, token source, bonus timing, overflow and project row distinction.

answers.answer: 1. Release categories are determined by the Animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement: 2− accepts size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5; the tile actually occupied or special-enclosure capacity does not change this. 2. First lose only that animal's printed Appeal and discard it, thereby losing its icons. Retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated Appeal, and earlier earned effects. 3. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you must remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or if none, the smallest meeting size alone; flip none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies to flock animals too. 4. Playing a new Release project gives 1 reputation; later supporting one already in play gives no such reputation.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild project rules spell out size categories, losses/retentions, enclosure freeing priority and new-card reputation.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly 1 hand Sponsor whose level is no greater than strength and whose conditions are met; alternatively advance Break by strength and take that much money. 2. Sponsors II may play multiple cards from hand and/or an in-range display; each display card costs its folder number extra, and conditions with the upgrade-required icon are allowed. The sum of card levels must be no greater than strength +1. Resolve each card's effects fully before playing the next, but defer “after finishing” effects to the end of the action. 3. If choosing the Break movement money option on Sponsors II, take money twice the strength. This is the full amount even if fewer Break spaces remain; any excess movement beyond the end is ignored.
answers.evidence: Sponsors action specifies side I/II level and source rules, effect order, and money option twice on side II; side I also says full money despite fewer spaces.

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit (3 normally, 5 with hand-limit university); remove Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and restock partner zoos/universities subject to ownership; discard folders 1–2, compact and refill display; take income; reset Break token. 2. Kiosk income is 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count, empty special enclosures do. 3. If several players take display cards during break income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them) and refill the display after each player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6 and kiosk income subsection state order, hand limits, qualifying neighbors, and clockwise/refill rule.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate another association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a nearby Bonus tile (if available), executing/removing a tile immediately. The first player reaching 10 makes every player discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if nobody reaches 10, all discard one before final scoring. 2. Check for game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or have passed one another. Appeal received during another player's turn is checked by its owner at the end of that owner's turn or a break. 3. The player who triggers end completes their turn; everyone else takes one more turn. If triggered during a break, all players get one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can give at most 4 additional conservation. Victory points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player with most conservation projects supported (tokens removed from map); remaining ties share victory.
answers.evidence: Conservation milestones, End of the game, and Final scoring sections give milestone rewards, check timing, extra turns, cap, formula and tiebreak.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place a random tile face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 conservation and two beside 8; do not use the two yellow icon spaces, and return the other 5 tiles to the box. 2. If component stock runs out, use a suitable substitute; physical stock alone does not forbid a legal play, though explicit per-zoo limits and board availability still apply.
answers.evidence: Global setup specifies randomized placement of four of nine tiles; component supply rule says use substitutes if stock runs out.

answers.answer: 1. Advanced Maps 1–8 are on reverse sides and each has an individual ability. Choose either 2 random zoo maps and select one advanced map, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose in reverse play order; return unselected maps to the box. 2. Map A begins with an empty size-3 enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built and a kiosk tile is placed over it as reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A gives both advanced-map selection methods and Map A starting enclosure/kiosk.

answers.answer: 1. Seven player tokens start on the designated spaces along the left edge of each zoo map and support conservation projects. 2. Hire inactive workers from the lowest supply space upward. 3. Some maps reward hiring the last worker with conservation points; the specific map determines whether that applies.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2 places 7 tokens at map's left edge; Association worker supply says hire lowest-up and certain maps grant conservation for last worker.

answers.answer: 1. On an upgrade, flip one side-I Action card of your choice to side II in its current slot. 2. Its improved action can be used from your next action, but it counts as upgraded immediately for conditions. 3. The summary says there are four upgrade opportunities and one allows an alternative, so you cannot upgrade all five cards.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards section states current position, next-action availability, immediate condition status, four ways and inability to upgrade all.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I draw / discard counts at strengths 1–5 are: 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1. 2. A required discard may be one of the cards just drawn or a card already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw tables and note specify side-I draw/discard table and eligible discard cards.

answers.answer: 1. The seven animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. Bears and Petting Zoo animals count as categories unless a rule explicitly excludes them; bear can also appear alongside herbivore or predator.
answers.evidence: Animal categories and Base glossary list all seven and clarify bears and Petting Zoo animals.

answers.answer: 1. Association II permits exactly 1 donation per Association action, only if at least 1 association task was also performed; no worker is needed for the donation. 2. Pay the smallest still-visible donation amount and cover that space with a player token from your supply to gain 1 conservation point. The printed ladder is 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then repeatable 12 money. 3. Skip spaces blocked at setup; after all spaces except the last are covered, each further donation costs 12 money and places no additional token.
answers.evidence: Association II donation paragraph gives conditions, amounts, token source, reward and repeatable space.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo icons include Animal and Sponsor upper-right icons; also count water/rock requirements at upper-left of Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards, plus partner-zoo continent and university research icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions or Conservation Project icons; university reputation and hand-limit symbols are benefits, not zoo icons. 3. A card counts its own icons for effects; doubled icons count twice, while repeated icons are one type when asked for different types. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo and shared principles state included/excluded icons, self-counting, doubled icons and card-text precedence.

answers.answer: 1. Count distinct water or rock hexes that are adjacent to the enclosure; multiple touching edges to the same terrain hex count once. A larger terrain region contributes only the hexes actually adjacent. 2. Water/rock illustrations printed on tiles are not terrain spaces and do not satisfy requirements.
answers.evidence: Terrain adjacency says count distinct adjacent hexes and decorative illustrations on tiles provide no terrain spaces.

answers.answer: 1. Only playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. 2. Every Breeding Program family card uses the same printed condition for all three reward spaces; if that condition is fulfilled, choose any available reward space.
answers.evidence: Release project rules distinguish play bonus from later support; Breeding Program cards 123–127 use same condition at all three levels and allow any available space.

answers.answer: 1. In “X : Y,” X is the condition and Y the reward. 2. A condition with no number or with “per” pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; if multiple thresholds appear, use the highest one met.
answers.evidence: Shared principles define X:Y condition/reward and how unnumbered, per, and numbered thresholds work.

answers.answer: 1. A connected space is uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map and personal supply; “any zoo” includes those areas for every player.
answers.evidence: Shared principles define connected, isolated, border space, your zoo and any zoo.

answers.answer: 1. Unique buildings enter only through their Sponsor cards, are placed when the Sponsor is played, use the matching tile with colored face up, may be freely rotated but not flipped, and have no size-based construction cost. Follow ordinary placement and any terrain requirements. 2. A unique building is not an enclosure, cannot house additional animals, and is not water or rock terrain. 3. If it cannot be legally placed, the Sponsor card cannot be played.
answers.evidence: Unique buildings rules specify placement, payment, orientation, enclosure/terrain status and inability to play card if placement impossible.

answers.answer: 1. For both a named Action and Determination (Any Action), finish Animals and move its card to slot 1 before taking the granted action. 2. Use the granted action's Action card normally, then move that card to slot 1 after it resolves. 3. A named Action cannot be replaced by the X-token alternative; Determination may choose any action, including the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications give shared timing/movement and distinguish named Action from Determination.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and takes the chosen project into hand; Dominance takes its named project from that deck. 2. Dominance has no effect if that named project is already in play. 3. Later play and immediately support the obtained card through Association, placing it above the Association board, not in the setup row below it.
answers.evidence: Assertion / Dominance clarification describes deck source, already-in-play exception, and later placement above the board.

answers.answer: 1. Boost and Clever resolve after the Animals action and its card have moved. 2. Clever places the chosen Action card in slot 1, shifting cards formerly to its left right. Boost puts the named card in slot 1 or slot 5; moving it to 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Boost / Clever clarification states timing, destinations and shift directions.

answers.answer: 1. An affected zoo must have at least 5 Appeal for these interactive effects. Venom affects every other zoo with higher Appeal; Constriction affects every other eligible zoo ahead of you on Appeal and/or Conservation; Hypnosis and Pilfering target leaders as specified below. 2. The playing animal's Appeal may be awarded before or after its ability, so its newly gained Appeal normally need not count when selecting the affected player. 3. In multiplayer, the group may use the solo replacement text on those ability cards instead; this does not require playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities: affected zoo at least 5 Appeal; the playing animal's Appeal may be before or after the ability; multiplayer group may replace with solo text.

answers.answer: 1. Constriction tokens go on each affected opponent's own Action cards: if ahead on one track, one token on its slot-5 card; if ahead on both Appeal and Conservation, one token on each of its slot-4 and slot-5 cards. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 2. Each affected action loses 2 strength, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. At effective strength 0 or less, spend enough X-tokens to reach 1, take the X-token alternative, or leave the card until at least slot 3. 3. Return a token after the card is acted with, or at break without effect.
answers.evidence: Constriction clarification specifies target card slots, no stacking, −2 action strength, multiplied actions, X-token/slot-3 options and token removal.

answers.answer: 1. A Constricted card at effective strength zero or below cannot be used as a regular action unless enough X-tokens are spent to bring it to at least 1. You can instead use the alternative X-token action, or leave that card until it is at least in slot 3. 2. The alternative X-token action is an option in this situation, subject to the normal five-token maximum.
answers.evidence: Constriction clarification: at effective strength zero or below use X-tokens to reach one, use alternative X-token action, or leave card until at least slot 3.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 allows up to two choices, and after each card you decide again which option to use; you can change options between selections. 2. A display card discarded through Digging is replenished immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification says choose up to twice between options and decide again after each card; display discard is replaced immediately.

answers.answer: 1. A Flock Animal may avoid occupying a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals. 3. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. 4. When releasing a flock animal, follow the release/fallback enclosure procedure; original residents need not be tracked or proven.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal clarification states host requirement, unlimited reuse, later non-flock restriction and no historical resident tracking.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. If your map grants conservation points for hiring your last worker, take that reward. 3. If all workers are already active, the ability has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated clarification specifies lowest reserve worker, last-worker map reward, and no effect if all active.

answers.answer: 1. If Hunter reveals no Animal card among the cards, discard all revealed cards; none is added to hand.
answers.evidence: Hunter X: with no Animal among revealed cards, discard all.

answers.answer: 1. Hypnosis targets a zoo tied for highest Appeal with at least 5 Appeal; choose among tied leaders. If your own zoo is the target, it has no effect. 2. Copy only a card in target slot 1, 2 or 3. Use the target card's upgraded or unupgraded side for the whole copied action; other action-card upgrade checks use your own cards. You may spend your own X-tokens. 3. Venom and Constriction on the targeted card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally. For copied action permissions, the copied card side controls that action's upgrades; e.g. borrowed Build II allows special enclosures/restricted spaces and borrowed Animals II allows upgrade-conditioned animals. Borrowed Association I retains its 2-partner limit. Unique buildings played via borrowed Sponsors still check your own Build side.
answers.evidence: Hypnosis clarification specifies target/ties/self, slots, card side and X-token ownership, applied tokens, Multiplier, movement and upgrade interactions.

answers.answer: 1. Place a gained Multiplier immediately on the named Action card if the reward names one; a Bonus tile lets you choose any Action card, including Animals. 2. On its next use, the action may be executed twice consecutively at the same base strength; move the card only after both. Each X-token boosts only one execution. Additional Multiplier tokens each add one execution, so two tokens allow up to three actions. 3. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions finish. A break caused by the first waits until the whole turn is over. 4. Return used tokens to supply; remove an unused token at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier section gives placement by source, executions, X-token treatment, deferred effects, break timing and return.

answers.answer: 1. Two Multiplier tokens allow up to three executions of that card's action, not four. 2. Each X-token boosts only one execution. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but you cannot mix one X-token action with one regular action.
answers.evidence: Multiplier section: additional tokens add one execution; X-token action can take two tokens but cannot mix regular and X-token alternative.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking allows the Large Bird Aviary to be placed before Build is upgraded; the zoo must not already have an Aviary and there must be a legal site. It does not waive other placement restrictions, including Build II for upgrade-marked map spaces. 2. Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and multiple buildings are placed one at a time.
answers.evidence: Peacocking/Posturing clarifications state exception, prerequisites, restrictions and sequential placement.

answers.answer: 1. Successive Petting Zoo animals grant 3, 6, then 9 Appeal. 2. A zoo's single Petting Zoo can hold at most three such animals. 3. Petting Zoo animals count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Petting Zoo animal clarification states first/second/third Appeal, one enclosure holds at most three, and they count as small.

answers.answer: 1. For Pilfering 1 and each separate Pilfering 2 selection, the acting player chooses among tied leaders. 2. A conservation target must have at least 1 Conservation; if every player has zero, Pilfering 2's conservation-target part has no effect, while its Appeal-target part still resolves normally. 3. A self-target has no effect.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X clarification details actor's tie choice, zero-conservation case and self-target.

answers.answer: 1. The target chooses whether to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. With no hand cards, the target gives 5 money; with less than 5 money, they give a card. With neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. 2. Resolve repeated Pilferings sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X specifies target chooses payment/card, card exclusions, shortages and sequential repeated resolution.

answers.answer: 1. Pouch may tuck up to X hand cards under the animal for 2 Appeal per card; tucked cards have no further function. If the animal is released, discard those tucked cards too, retaining the Appeal already gained. 2. Sunbathing X may sell up to X hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Pouch X and Sunbathing X clarifications state payment, function, release and discard destination.

answers.answer: 1. If Resistance gives an extra Final Scoring card before the 10-conservation milestone, it joins the cards from which you choose one to discard at that milestone. 2. At game end score every Final Scoring card remaining, each capped at 4 additional conservation.
answers.evidence: Resistance clarification says extra card joins milestone choices and all remaining cards score separately under four-point cap.

answers.answer: 1. Scavenging shuffles the discard pile face down, draws the specified number randomly, makes the card's stated selection, then returns the discard pile face up. For illustrated Scavenging 3, draw three random cards, keep one and discard the other two.
answers.evidence: Scavenging clarification gives random face-down selection, restoration, and Scavenging 3 example.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; drawing from the deck is not an alternative. 2. Sponsor Magnet selects display Sponsors without a reputation-range restriction; if none are present, it has no effect. 3. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping / Sponsor Magnet clarification states source, range, empty result and refill timing.

answers.answer: 1. Venom targets every other zoo with more Appeal than the acting player, subject to the 5-Appeal floor. Put tokens on cards in that target's lowest slots (1, then 2), at most one per card; return duplicates. 2. Using a card with Venom removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including using the X-token alternative if you have fewer than five X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one remains. If unable, undo the turn and choose another action; spending all money does not avoid the fee. The next break clears unused tokens without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom clarification covers target, placement/stacking, use, turn-end fee and break expiry.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian gives 2/5/10 money for having 1/2/3 universities when played. 2. While in play, conservation-project work requires Association strength 4 instead of 5. 3. Its final reward is 1 Conservation for three universities.
answers.evidence: 203 Veterinarian entry gives immediate university-based money, project-work strength 4 and final reward.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough gains 2 Appeal per previously supported project, counted by the player tokens missing from the left edge of the owner's map. 2. It gives 1 Conservation at each break.
answers.evidence: 206 Medical Breakthrough entry specifies missing-map-token count and break income.

answers.answer: 1. On play, count distinct continent and animal-category icon types together, excluding research icons; repeated and doubled copies count only once per type. Gain 1 Conservation per two types, rounding down. 2. Each other player gains 2 money for every Conservation point you gain.
answers.evidence: 207 Basic Research entry specifies icon types, rounding, and other players' money.

answers.answer: 1. On play, Science Library gives 1 Appeal per research icon. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final condition gives 1 Conservation if its owner has five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: 208 Science Library entry states all three effects.

answers.answer: 1. On play, gain 1 Appeal per Americas icon. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk under normal placement and spacing rules. 3. Its final reward is 1 Conservation with five or more kiosks.
answers.evidence: 210 Expert on Americas entry states immediate reward, free kiosk rule and final condition; general kiosk spacing applies to every new kiosk.

answers.answer: 1. On play, gain 1 Appeal per Australia icon. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card under this Sponsor for 2 Appeal; tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: 212 Expert on Australia entry specifies immediate and recurring effect; tucked cards have no further function.

answers.answer: 1. When played, take two player tokens from your supply and place them on this Sponsor's two top spaces. 2. When supporting a base project below the Association board, you may return exactly one of these tokens to your supply as any one icon; you cannot spend both on the same project. A card originating as a base project but later played above the board does not qualify. 3. Final scoring gives 1 Conservation with five or more project supports, counted by missing left-map tokens.
answers.evidence: 215/218 Breeding Program entry specifies stored tokens, qualifying base projects, spending limit and final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Each Build action may include one extra copy of a building already built in that same action, without additional strength; pay its normal cost and follow normal placement. Only one extra building is allowed even if several different buildings were built, and special-enclosure one-per-type limits still apply. 2. Engineer's final reward is 5 Appeal with a full map except water/rock.
answers.evidence: 217 Engineer entry gives duplicate construction exception, cost/placement/limit and final reward.

answers.answer: 1. On play, Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon. 2. It lets you build over water/rock and ignore animal and unique-building terrain requirements; printed terrain icons still count, and water/rock need not be covered for full-map scoring. 3. Covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo. 4. Final scoring gives 2 Appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, up to three pairs.
answers.evidence: 219 Diversity Researcher entry gives immediate reward, terrain permissions/counting exceptions and final score.

answers.answer: 1. Each actual placement bonus on a border space triggers an additional choice of any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily on the border. Multiple border bonuses create multiple extra choices; copied bonuses may be same or different, resolved in chosen order. 2. An H space or other non-placement bonus does not trigger it; simultaneous actual triggers may choose the same uncovered bonus. 3. Final condition: 1 Conservation when all building border spaces are covered, excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: 221 Archaeologist states border-placement triggers, any uncovered bonus and repeat selection; Hollywood Hills says H is not placement bonus; final reward stated.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. Each Release into the Wild support grants 1 additional Conservation. You may support the same release project repeatedly with different qualifying animals, but at most once on that project per Association action. 3. Each token placed counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: 224 Migration Recording entry specifies immediate token, release bonus, repeated support limit and support counting.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. It makes its owner immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore the owner's counters and choose the next qualifying player. 3. Its final condition gives 1 Conservation with all five continents.
answers.evidence: 225 Quarantine Lab entry states immediate reward, immunity/redirect and final condition.

answers.answer: 1. Choose small or large permanently and mark that choice with a supply token. Reveal deck cards until finding an Animal of that type; keep it and discard the others. 2. You may not play the opposite type. Small animals you choose gain 2 extra Appeal each; large animals gain 4. Size-3 animals remain legal but get no bonus.
answers.evidence: 227 WAZA Special Assignment entry specifies selection, reveal, prohibition and size rewards.

answers.answer: 1. On play, WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal. 2. When an Animals action consists only of small animals, you may play one additional small animal from hand using normal costs/rules, then take one small animal from the display into hand regardless of reputation. You may take the display animal even if you declined the extra play. 3. Mixing small and large animals in the original action prevents the effect.
answers.evidence: 228 entry specifies immediate reward, all-small action requirement and extra hand/display acquisition.

answers.answer: 1. On play, Hydrologist gives 1 Appeal per water icon. 2. Each newly covered space adjacent to water gives 1 money, even multiple spaces of one building; a space touching multiple water hexes pays only once. 3. Final reward is 1 Conservation if all water hexes are connected, with none isolated.
answers.evidence: 241 Hydrologist entry specifies each effect.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut places its unique building. 2. Whenever a bird icon is played, draw two cards from the deck, keep one and discard the other.
answers.evidence: 249 Barred Owl Hut entry gives placement and recurring draw effect.

answers.answer: 1. Place Sea Turtle Tank adjacent to water. 2. Whenever a reptile icon is played, you may sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: 250 Sea Turtle Tank entry specifies placement and recurring sale.

answers.answer: 1. Whenever a predator icon is played, Spotted Hyena Compound uses Hunter with a number of draws equal to your total predator icons. 2. A newly played card with two predator icons triggers two sequential Hunter effects, counting both new icons each time.
answers.evidence: 252 Spotted Hyena Compound entry gives Hunter count and duplicate-icon sequence.

answers.answer: 1. Place Okapi Stable and three supply tokens on its card. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a Sponsor's level to play a Sponsor from your hand, following normal conditions. 2. The Stable's own herbivore icon can trigger this when played; there are three uses total.
answers.evidence: 253 Okapi Stable entry states setup, per-icon use, price/card source/conditions and self-trigger.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School gives 1 Reputation and 1 Conservation; place its building covering at least two border spaces. 2. Also take one in-range display card or draw one deck card. Resolve simultaneous benefits in your chosen order.
answers.evidence: 254 Zoo School entry states rewards, placement and card source choices.

answers.answer: 1. Place Side Entrance on two border spaces; it need not touch an existing building, but other placement rules apply. Later buildings may attach to it. 2. At breaks it gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures. It can stand beside a kiosk, and as a unique building it counts for adjacent kiosk income. 3. Final reward is 5 Appeal with a full map excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: 257 Side Entrance entry states placement exception, income and full-map reward; kiosk note confirms it counts as a building.

answers.answer: 1. On play, Native Farm Animals gives 1 Appeal per connected uncovered building border space; water and rock spaces never count. 2. Final scoring gives 1 Conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluating each group separately. Restricted spaces count even without Build II; water/rock do not. The example groups 13, 6, 3, 2 yield 3 total.
answers.evidence: 260 Native Farm Animals entry specifies both scoring effects, spaces included/excluded and example.

answers.answer: 1. On play, Explorer gives 2 money per different continent/animal-category icon; research icons do not count. 2. Each category or continent newly introduced to your zoo gives 1 Appeal and 2 money. A newly played double identical icon earns this novelty bonus only once.
answers.evidence: 262 Explorer entry states immediate count, new icon reward and duplicate handling.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program lets you place one size-5 standard enclosure free under normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, ignore one left-side condition, such as a required icon or Animals upgrade; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: 263 WAZA Large Animal Program entry gives building and condition waiver; Map 6 Research Institute explains stacking.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo gives 1 Conservation for each animal category where your zoo has more icons than the player to your right, up to 4 Conservation. 2. If the neighbor has zero icons in a category, one of your icons is enough to exceed them.
answers.evidence: Biodiverse Zoo 009 clarification states comparison, zero-category rule and cap.

answers.answer: 1. Observation Tower's bonus applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not merely another rock hex. 2. An animal housed there gives the two Appeal again even if an earlier animal was released. Special enclosures get no effect. 3. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1 Observation Tower clarification provides adjacency, repeat effect, special enclosure exclusion and building status.

answers.answer: 1. A standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex counts as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; adjacency to another water hex is insufficient. 2. This adjusted size also applies on release or transfer and cannot be ignored (e.g. physical size 2 counts as size 4). 3. It does not affect special enclosures, and Outdoor Areas is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2 Outdoor Areas clarification specifies adjacency, size effect, release/transfer, special enclosure and building status.

answers.answer: 1. A building on the space adjacent to Commercial Harbor connects/activates it; your first building may start beside Harbor but need not. 2. Its discard ability can be used before, during or after your action, only once on your own turn, never during a break or another player's turn. 3. Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4 Commercial Harbor clarification states activation, first building, timing/frequency and status.

answers.answer: 1. Park Restaurant's own break income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, regardless of building type or occupancy; empty enclosures count, and each adjacent hex counts separately even within one building. 2. The Restaurant is not a building and contributes no income to adjacent kiosks. 3. Its special-enclosure bonus grants one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, chosen between them, even before Build II; other normal placement rules still apply.
answers.evidence: Map 5 Park Restaurant clarification specifies income calculation, kiosk treatment and free special-enclosure choice.

answers.answer: 1. Cover each H space by placing a building under ordinary placement rules; when covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears, keep it and discard the others. H is not a placement bonus and does not trigger Archaeologist. 2. After all three H spaces are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 3. Its partner-zoo bonuses still require Association II for the third/fourth partner, and bonus buildings still require Build II for upgrade-marked spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8 Hollywood Hills clarification specifies H resolution, Archaeologist, completed bonus and persistent upgrades.

answers.answer: 1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its normal play conditions. 2. Play the Sponsor only from hand, even with Sponsors II. 3. The bonus leaves the Sponsors Action card in its current slot; it does not move it.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ Sponsor-play bonus specifies level payment, normal conditions, hand-only source and no Action-card movement.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and Conservation cannot exceed 41; further gains beyond those track ends are lost. Reputation has a separate overflow rule: above 15 it converts to 1 Appeal per step.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ states Appeal 113 and Conservation 41 caps; reputation overflow defined in track rules.

answers.answer: 1. All affected zoos need at least 5 Appeal. Venom affects every other zoo with higher Appeal than yours. Constriction affects every other eligible zoo ahead of you on Appeal and/or Conservation. 2. Hypnosis targets the highest-Appeal zoo among those with at least 5 Appeal; choose among ties, and it has no effect if you are the target. Copy only slots 1, 2 or 3. 3. Pilfering 1 targets a highest-Appeal zoo, choosing tied leaders; self-target has no effect. Pilfering 2 separately targets a highest-Appeal zoo and a most-Conservation zoo; each needs at least 5 Appeal, the Conservation target needs at least 1 Conservation, ties are chosen separately, a self-target has no effect, and one zoo may be targeted twice. 4. Constriction puts one token on each target's slot-5 card if ahead on one track; if ahead on both, put one on each slot-4 and slot-5 card (never stack).
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference and detailed ability clarifications specify all thresholds, targets, ties, Hypnosis slots and Constriction token counts.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal partner-zoo condition requires a partner from that animal's continent; a Sponsor partner-zoo condition allows a partner from any continent. 2. A red maximum-25-Appeal condition allows play only while Appeal is 25 or lower; the marker at 25 is a reminder, not a general cap. 3. A minimum-Reputation condition requires at least its printed value. 4. The summary does not explain a minus-one-condition bonus; that specific symbol/ruling is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ defines Animal/Sponsor partner conditions, red Appeal maximum and minimum reputation; no minus-one-condition rule is stated.

answers.answer: 1. Crested Porcupine's Digging 2 provides up to two selections, each choosing between discarding a display card and immediately replenishing it, or discarding a hand card and drawing one deck card. 2. Decide separately after each selection, so the two options can differ.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 (illustrated Crested Porcupine) specifies these two choices and “up to twice.”

answers.answer: 1. After display cards are taken, slide cards from higher-numbered folders down while keeping their order, then fill the remaining empty folders from the deck. The display is replenished at turn end.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display says move higher-numbered cards down keeping order, then fill empty spaces from deck.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures with the empty side up, showing the yellow border and size number. 2. Each placement-bonus icon covered is gained immediately once; turning that enclosure occupied later does not award the covered placement bonus again.
answers.evidence: Build action says standard enclosure is placed empty side up; placement bonus is immediate once and not awarded again on occupancy.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches or exceeds 10 conservation, each player discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining Final Scoring pile.
answers.evidence: Conservation track milestone says all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; play proceeds clockwise. 2. There are no formal rounds: players take turns one at a time until the end is triggered. 3. On a regular turn, take one action using one of the five Action cards; additional granted effects/actions resolve as specified after or during that action.
answers.evidence: Global setup says randomly determine start player and clockwise order; Overview says no formal rounds; Turn Structure says one action per turn.

answers.answer: 1. If no player reaches 10 conservation before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
answers.evidence: Conservation track milestone states if nobody reaches 10 before game end, all discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring.
